summary.text: Aaron Bean is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Florida's 4th District, first elected in 2022. Before Congress he was a community bank president and small-business founder, mayor of Fernandina Beach, and a Florida state representative and senator. He is seeking a third term and sits on the House Ways and Means Committee.

paragraphs.text: Born in Fernandina Beach, Florida, in 1967. According to his congressional website, he grew up as the youngest of nine children in a working-class family, the grandson of a coal miner and the son of teachers.
Graduated from high school in 1985 and earned a B.S. in finance from Jacksonville University in 1989.

Worked as an auctioneer and as a relationship development officer with UF Health Jacksonville. His congressional website says he was a community bank president and built four small businesses, including the High Energy Auction Company.
Began in public office as a city commissioner and then mayor of his hometown of Fernandina Beach, serving 1996-1999.

Served in the Florida House of Representatives (2000-2008) and the Florida Senate (2012-2022); in the Senate he was President Pro Tempore and chaired the Appropriations Subcommittee on Health and Human Services, according to his congressional website.
Won the open U.S. House seat in 2022 (60.5% to Democrat LaShonda Holloway), succeeding John Rutherford, and took office January 3, 2023; he was re-elected in 2024.

Chaired the Early Childhood, Elementary, and Secondary Education subcommittee of the Committee on Education and the Workforce, and served on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Small Business, during the 118th Congress (2023-2024); in the 119th Congress (2025-2026) he sits on the Committee on Ways and Means, including the Subcommittees on Social Security, Work and Welfare, and Oversight.
Describes himself as the founder and co-chair of the Delivering Outstanding Government Efficiency (DOGE) Caucus, which he says works to reduce government fraud, waste, and abuse.
According to his congressional website, he and his wife, Abby, have three sons and a granddaughter born in 2024.
